explanation: Relocation entries are crucial in the linking and loading process.  When an object file is compiled, addresses of functions and data are often unknown.  The linker assigns final addresses.  Relocation entries within the object file specify which memory locations need to be adjusted (patched) after the linker has assigned final addresses. This ensures that references within the code and data sections point to the correct locations in the loaded program's memory space.  Without relocation, linking would be impossible, as code would contain incorrect memory addresses, leading to runtime crashes.
keywords: Relocation, Linker relocation, Relocation entry, Address patching
